note: Copies of one bank alert across mailboxes (and within one, after a reconnect). A v4 txn_ingested may carry dedupe {message_id, bank_ref}: 32 lower-case hex digits each (message_id is the first 16 bytes of SHA-256 over the RFC 5322 Message-ID, angle brackets dropped, ASCII lower-cased). A certain copy (a dedupe key already in byDedupeKey on a live row) merges at once: the copy whose gates say ar pass and sender trusted wins, else the earlier one; the other gets merged_into, merge_kind certain and merge_op, leaves the live indexes, and becomes an alias on the canonical row. Re-ingesting a merged copy's ingest id is a duplicate_ingest. A probable copy (no shared key; both mailbox rows at time precision with the same bank, amount_minor, currency, direction, last4 and merchant after ASCII lower-casing and white-space folding, at most 600000 ms apart) gets copy_of the earliest live match and stays out of money until txn_copy_resolved {other_txn_id, decision: merge | keep_both | null}. Written by the Swift executor; the TypeScript reference (schema 3) and Go (no fold) do not model v4.
format: Each case is a conformance/replay case (log items of ops, expect.state blanked as there, expect.state_sha256 the pass condition), folded by the v4 fold.

cases.name: certain-merge
cases.note: The same alert in two mailboxes shares its Message-ID: one row stays, the other is its alias; neither sender verified, so the earlier import is canonical.

cases.name: verified-wins
cases.note: The later copy's sender verified and the earlier one's did not: the later copy is canonical and the earlier row becomes its alias.

cases.name: reconnect-rescan-no-readd
cases.note: After a reconnect the same message is read again under the same ingest id: it is refused as duplicate_ingest, and the alias list does not grow.

cases.name: probable-hold
cases.note: No shared id; same bank, amount, card and merchant (case and spacing differ) five minutes apart: the second is held as a copy. Eleven minutes apart, or one fils different, stays separate.

cases.name: keep-both
cases.note: The held copy is kept as its own transaction: copy_decision keep_both, counted again.

cases.name: merge-then-undo
cases.note: Merge makes the held copy an alias (merge_kind user); the undo (decision null) brings it back as a held copy, live and indexed again.

cases.name: two-identical-coffees
cases.note: Two real coffees, same card, same amount, three minutes apart, from one mailbox: the second is held, Keep both makes it count, and both stay as two rows; a merge of the kept row with the wrong other row is refused.

cases.name: retire-promotes-the-copy
cases.note: Removing the canonical row's mailbox brings its alias from the other mailbox back as the live row, with the dedupe key; a copy held against the removed row is released.

cases.name: verified-wins-keeps-the-sort
cases.note: The earlier, unverified copy was sorted (txn_categorized, source user) and noted before the verified copy arrived: the verified copy is canonical and takes the sort (category, category_source, needs_review) and the annotations it lacks.

cases.name: retire-promotes-the-sort
cases.note: The canonical row was sorted, then its mailbox was removed: the alias brought back as the live row keeps the sort.
